description:
The transfer arc drawn for some missions looks wrong — the endpoints are in the right places but the middle of the arc has the wrong shape.

## Reporter answers (follow-up)

Q: Which specific missions look wrong? (IDs, or screenshots showing expected vs actual.)
A: I don't know. My notes don't include specific mission IDs or screenshots.

Q: What shape is expected instead — a standard Hohmann half-ellipse, a Lambert-solved true transfer, or a different Keplerian arc?
A: The expected shape is a baseline ellipse that gets visibly bent in the middle when the arrival V-infinity is high, while both endpoints stay pinned to the transfer points. A low/zero arrival V-infinity leaves the arc close to the baseline ellipse.

Q: Is the discrepancy on /fly (transferEllipse) or on /explore (outboundArc)? Two different functions with different endpoint-pinning strategies.
A: I don't know. My notes don't mention /fly, transferEllipse, /explore, or outboundArc.

Q: Is the perceived error that the arc looks 'too flat' / 'too curved' / 'asymmetric'? This distinguishes V∞ shaping absence (always symmetric Hohmann) from a geometry bug.
A: The error is that the mid-arc bend is wrong — the arrival V-infinity is not being applied at all. The arc always looks like the baseline ellipse regardless of the arrival V-infinity value. For missions with high arrival V-infinity, the arc should visibly bend away from that baseline in the middle, but it doesn't.

Q: Does the issue reproduce for every mission at a particular destination (e.g., all Venus missions) or only missions with flight.arrival.v_infinity_km_s?
A: It affects missions that have a meaningful arrival V-infinity in their data. It is not tied to a particular destination.
